title: Reachability across a cleared register
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathsf{orc}$ assign a Boolean to each of four query types and each finite bit string, and let $x$ be a finite bit string. Let $st$ be a machine state whose 17 register values are all at most $B$, let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory function, and let $p\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $0\le p\le P$. If the machine's instruction at state $l$ clears register $r$ and moves to state $l'$, and there is a finite guarded run from state $l'$ with register vector obtained from $st$ by setting register $r$ to zero, memory $M$, and memory head at $p$, to a configuration $c$, then there is such a guarded run from state $l$ with register vector $st$, the same memory and head position, to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle with four query types and finite bit-string inputs
State $st$ has all 17 register values at most $B$
Instruction at $l$ clears register $r$ and goes to $l'$
A guarded finite run exists from the cleared-register configuration to $c$
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let an oracle assign Boolean answers to four query
types and finite bit strings, and let $x$ be a bit string. Suppose $st$ is a machine
state, $M$ is a memory, $p$ is an integer with $0\le p\le P$, and clearing register $r$
at state $l$ leads to state $l'$. If the bounded-reachability property holds from the
configuration with state $l'$, registers obtained from $st$ by setting register $r$ to
zero, memory $M$, and head position $p$, then it also holds from the configuration with
state $l$, registers given by $st$, memory $M$, and head position $p$. Here $st$ has
every register at most $B$.
